cues.text: A boy who loved the ball
Vinícius Júnior was born in 2000 in São Gonçalo, near Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil.
His family did not have much money.
When he was six, his father took him to a football school run by the club Flamengo, near their home.
Kick the ball.
Vinícius played futsal there, the fast, small-sided game, before he chose football.
Futsal is played on a hard court with a smaller ball, and it teaches quick feet and fast thinking.
Those skills stayed with him.
You don’t need much to start. A ball and a chance can be enough.
Help from his family
In 2010, Vinícius had a trial for Flamengo’s youth team, and he was accepted.
But the training ground was a long way from home.
Getting there every day would have been very hard.
Open the door.
Vinícius moved in with his uncle Ulisses, to be closer to training.
The club and some local business people also helped the family with money.
Many people helped one boy chase his dream.
The people who help you are part of your team.
A big move, and big pressure
Vinícius played his first match for Flamengo’s first team at sixteen.
Real Madrid agreed to sign him, and in 2018, when he was eighteen, he moved to Spain.
Moving to a new country at eighteen, with a new language, is a big change.
Lift the flap.
Some people said his shooting was not good enough.
Vinícius kept practising, and he kept getting better.
He worked on his shooting and his decisions in front of goal.
When people criticise you, use it to practise, not to give up.
The winning goal
In May 2022, Real Madrid played Liverpool in the Champions League final, in Paris.
Vinícius scored the only goal of the game.
Millions of people were watching around the world.
Flip the scoreboard.
Real Madrid won 1–0 and were the champions of Europe.
The player people had doubted had scored the winning goal in the biggest club final of all.
Keep believing in yourself, even when others doubt you.
Speaking up
In Spain, some people in football crowds abused Vinícius because of the colour of his skin.
This is called racism, and it is always wrong.
Nobody should ever be treated badly because of how they look.
Raise the banner.
Vinícius did not stay quiet.
He spoke up and asked for stronger action.
In Brazil, new laws named after him allow matches to be stopped when there is racist abuse, and FIFA asked him to lead a group of players working against racism.
Racism is never okay. Speaking up, and standing with people treated unfairly, takes courage.
Helping children learn
In 2021, Vinícius started the Instituto Vini Jr., which helps children and teenagers from poor neighbourhoods in Brazil to go to school and keep learning.
Vinícius had grown up in a family without much money.
Open the book.
In 2024, UNESCO, part of the United Nations, made him a Goodwill Ambassador for education.
He was only the second Brazilian footballer to do this job, after Pelé.
That December, FIFA named him The Best Men’s Player in the world.
Use what you have to help others. Learning opens doors.
